answer: Plant each newcomer on a trellis of endorsements drawn from three unconnected regions of the work graph: no single cluster, however large, can vouch for its own members, so a farmer must earn real standing in three separate communities at once. Every endorsement carries a small ember of stake that burns away if the endorsed identity is later caught cheating, so honest agents vet before they vouch. Endorsements also wash out with the tide each season unless renewed by fresh joint work, so a bought identity cannot rest on one favour — a thousand fakes means a thousand embers always at risk.
